title: Operator eyeball cleanroom: observability housekeeping playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operator-focused playbook for daily/weekly observability housekeeping. Target audience: oncall operators, SREs, and PMs doing fast dashboard sprints.

Context / rationale:
- Our observability deck has grown organically; many panels are low-signal but high-query-cost. Need a light-weight ritual that mixes human eyeballs + simple heuristics to keep the surface area useful.
- This doc is intentionally practical: a set of small checks and definitions that fit a 15–30 minute daily run, plus a weekly "cleanroom" session for pruning.
- Emphasis: keep traces linkable to panels, reduce panel cardinality explosion, and protect probe budget for rollout smoke tests.

Daily operator checklist (15 min):
1) Eyeball the top-5 latency outliers panel (last 1h) — flag any persistent tail beyond p95 baseline.
2) Check synthetic-probe heartbeat (probe-success-rate >= 99.5% last 15m). If degraded, open OBS-quick incident and annotate probe payload.
3) Review any new alerts fired in the last 12h — triage to: config flapping / infra noise / genuine regression.
4) Spot-check one model-route panel (rotate daily) for token-cost, time-to-first-token, and error-rate drift.
5) Quick trace-linked check: pick one slow request trace and confirm the trace includes kvcache and router spans. If missing, tag the trace as "missing-span" and add note.

Weekly cleanroom (45–75 min):
- Team: 2 operators + 1 owning engineer. Goal: prune or annotate panels that score low on the Sparseness metric (see below).
- Steps:
  a) Run the dashboard query-cost report for the week (auto-export).
  b) For each panel with weekly-query-cost in top 30% but median-signal below threshold, either compress timeframe, reduce groups, or retire.
  c) Update panel with a Trace Anchor: a short note with an example trace id and steps to reproduce.
  d) Close loop with owning engineer by opening a small PR to rename / tag panel status.

Key heuristics and small definitions (single-line definitions to use during run):
- Sparseness score = (unique_label_count / sample_count) * cardinality_penalty. Aim: panels with Sparseness > 0.25 need attention.
- Trace anchor: the canonical span id + 2-line description stored in panel description. Helps operators find representative traces.
- Eyeball baseline: p95 over last 7 days. If current p95 > baseline * 1.18 => label "possible-regression".
- Probe weight: synthetic probes count as 3x a single alert sample when allocating sampling budget.

Practical metric definitions (copyable lines for panel descriptions):
- request.latency_ms: time from request-received to final-token-emitted (median/p95/p99) — exclude retries.
- ttf_token_ms: time from request-received to first-token-streamed (median / p95).
- kvcache.hit_rate: hits / (hits + misses) per model-version, 5m window.
- route.error_rate: non-2xx-per-1000-requests per route, 1m window; stratify by tenant.
- probe.success_rate: synthetic probe pass ratio, 15m and 24h windows.
- token.cost_per_request: tokens_consumed * token_unit_price — same currency as billing export.

Trace design notes / minimal span contract (for fast debugging):
- Required spans for token-serving flow: client -> router -> model-infer -> kvcache (optional) -> response-assemble.
- Each span must include: trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, tenant_id, model_id, model_version, request_id, token_count (if applicable).
- router span should annotate routing_decision: {primary_model, fallback_model, reason}.
- model-infer span should emit kernel_selection hint and nvtx-tag (if available) for local debug correlation.

Sampling and retention quick rules:
- Default adaptive sampling: keep 100% traces for errors and latencies > p99; sample successful traces at 2–5% per route, with heavier sampling for top-tenants.
- Apply privacy scrub: large user_text blobs must be redacted at ingest and replaced with a 16-byte hash; full text available only in air-gapped customer workspaces.
- Retention tiers: 30d full traces, 90d aggregated metrics. For customer-investigation bundles, create anchor exports to S3.

Dashboard slimming playbook (concrete ops actions):
- Rename panels to include owner shortcode (e.g., "serving:pl"), timeframe and scope. Short names = faster eyeballing.
- Add a one-line "what to do" in panel description: e.g., "If spike: open OBS-1423, attach trace id."
- Reduce dimensioning: do not show more than 6 columns in a single table panel. If >6, create a cohort panel per tenant-tier.
- Replace heavy ad-hoc SQL panels with precomputed metric rollups where possible (5m rollup recommended).

Synthetic probe design (for rollout smoke and region checks):
- Probe types: sanity (does the model start + respond), quality (token distribution sanity), latency (cold-start TTF).
- Probe cadence: regional sanity probes every 15s, quality probes every 5m, rollout stress probes (burst) only during rollout window.
- Attach metadata to probe spans: probe_id, probe_type, target_model, region, commit_hash.
- Failure taxonomy: transient(>1m, <5m) vs persistent(>15m) — configure alert thresholds accordingly.

Runbook snippets (copy into runbook tool):
- If p95 latency spike + probe failure: check KV eviction dashboard -> if kvcache hit_rate drops >10% then escalate to infra.
- If model-infer error rate increases and traces show kernel-selection=N/A: flag model-compiler team, tag PR.

Operator quickcards (two-liners to paste into Slack):
- "Observed: p95 serving latency up 25% on route X; probe-success 96%. Next: grab a slow trace, check kvcache hit_rate and router fallback_count."
- "Action: run synthetic-quality probe (manually) with last-good-prompt and attach trace id to ticket."

Compact SQL snippets (for quick reuse):
- Top slow routes last hour: SELECT route, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95 FROM metrics WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY route ORDER BY p95 desc LIMIT 25;
- Sparseness candidate panels: SELECT panel_id, weekly_query_cost, median_signal FROM dashboard_cost WHERE weekly_query_cost > 1000 AND median_signal < 0.02;

Ownership and small process rules:
- Every dashboard must list an owner in the title and have an "obs:oncall" collaborator. Owners must respond to a panel flagged in Cleanroom within 5 business days.
- PRs that retire or significantly change panels must include a short blurb: reason + expected savings (query_cost / week).

Open questions / unresolved things (agenda for next cleanroom):
- What should the exact Sparseness threshold be per tenant-tier? (measurement required across last 3 months).
- Do we need a separate probe set for quantized model variants (observability differences)?
- Explore automated trace-anchoring: can we embed the top-ranked trace id into the panel via the widgets API?

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Implement Sparseness calc in the dashboard-cost job (OBS-1423). Owner: Ben Chu.
- [ ] Add trace-anchor field to 25 highest-cost panels. Owner: Lena.
- [ ] Run first weekly cleanroom Jan 22, invite serving runtime + console PMs.

Notes to self (roughs, leave in doc):
- Keep language operator-friendly; avoid deep metrics-first walls. Operators are biased to do quick action; the playbook should enable that.
- Consider a small Slack bot to post the daily quickcheck summary and pin the panel links.

Reference links and tickets:
- OBS-1423 (dashboard-cost / sparseness work)
- OBS-1598 (probe tagging / retention)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-playbooks/pull/22 (panel cleanup template)

End of doc.

-- Aisha
